annotation.title_clean: Principles of cyber security for connected and automated vehicles
annotation.title_en: Principles of cyber security for connected and automated vehicles
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Centre for the Protection of National Infrastructure; Centre for Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (UK Government)
annotation.summary_en: UK government (CPNI and CCAV) guidance page, published August 2017, setting out eight principles for cyber security of connected and automated vehicles. The principles apply across the automotive supply chain and call for board-level ownership, proportionate risk management, defence-in-depth, lifetime software security, secure data and resilient systems.
key_provisions_or_claims: Organisational security is owned, governed and promoted at board level
Security risks, including supply-chain risks, are assessed and managed proportionately
Product aftercare and incident response ensure systems stay secure over their lifetime
Systems use defence-in-depth and manage software security throughout its lifetime
Data storage and transmission are secure, and systems stay resilient when defences or sensors fail
